title: Metformin and insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a mechanistic review
text: Metformin remains the first-line pharmacological therapy for type 2 diabetes mellitus. Its principal mechanism of action involves activation of AMP-activated protein kinase, which increases peripheral insulin sensitivity and reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis. Unlike sulfonylureas, metformin does not stimulate insulin secretion and therefore carries a low risk of hypoglycemia when used as monotherapy. Long-term studies have also associated metformin use with modest cardiovascular benefit and weight neutrality.
